first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both currently declining, and simplifying onboarding has prior evidence of improving completion, time-to-value, and early adoption—drivers of sustainable qualified revenue. A guarded test limits the risk that simplification reduces qualification or data quality. Verify the pricing and onboarding evidence because promotional pricing is highly consequential given the competitor move, while onboarding evidence directly supports the intended intervention.

final.rationale: Run a standard, guarded onboarding-simplification experiment. The verified shortened-flow result improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing the concurrent completion and activation declines with evidence consistent with durable qualified revenue. Include qualification, activation, and retention guardrails so reduced data collection or lower-friction signup does not degrade downstream account quality. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified acquisition and qualified-revenue lift came with a 12% 30-day retention decline, making it unsuitable for the sustainable-revenue objective despite the competitor's pricing move.
